body.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal Z\ne\varnothing\), \(m\) is odd, every arrow \(j\to i\) in \(G\) satisfies \(j<i\), \(u\to v\in G\), and
\[
 \kappa\le m(1-\gamma)^{m-1}.
\]
Then the derivative-separated regular class \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}^{\partial}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max},\kappa)\) is nonempty.  Uniformly over this class, as \(n\to\infty\), the real vector stacking the real and imaginary parts of
\[
 \sqrt n\bigl(\widehat h_{uv}(z)-h_{uv}(z)\bigr),
 \qquad z\in\mathcal Z,
\]
converges to the centered Gaussian law obtained by applying the Jacobian of the moment-to-root recursion and
\[
 \mathrm dh_{uv}(z)
 =\frac{z\,\mathrm dA_{vu}}{1-A_{vv}z}
  +\frac{A_{vu}z^2\,\mathrm dA_{vv}}{(1-A_{vv}z)^2}
\]
to the long-run Gaussian lag-moment covariance.  Let \(\widehat\Sigma_h\) be the positive-semidefinite plug-in estimate obtained from the Gaussian Isserlis covariance series and the recursive Jacobian, and let \(\widehat c_{1-\alpha}\) be the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of the maximum complex modulus of the corresponding centered Gaussian vector.  Then
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}^{\partial}}
 \left|
 P\!\left\{
 h_{uv}(z)\in
 \left\{w\in\mathbb C:
 |w-\widehat h_{uv}(z)|\le
 \frac{\widehat c_{1-\alpha}}{\sqrt n}
 \right\}
 \text{ for every }z\in\mathcal Z
 \right\}-(1-\alpha)
 \right|\longrightarrow0,
\]
where the class in the supremum has the full argument list displayed above.
body.justification: The globally separated theorem is preserved as a simple nonvacuous corollary of the sharper target-corridor result.
body.gap: Global regularity is stronger than the target requires, but remains an easily stated sufficient condition.
body.consumer: Existing implementations that already recover the full triangular root may continue to use the global estimator and obtain the same target bands.
body.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 \mathfrak P_{\partial}
 =\mathcal M_{\mathrm{reg}}^{\partial}
 (d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max},\kappa)
\]
and let \(\mathfrak P_{uv,\partial}\) denote the target-corridor class in
\(\mathrm{def{:}corridor\mbox{-}derivative\mbox{-}separated\mbox{-}class}\),
with the same displayed arguments.  By
\(\mathrm{def{:}regular\mbox{-}class}\) and
\(\mathrm{def{:}derivative\mbox{-}separated\mbox{-}regular\mbox{-}class}\),
each \(P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}\) belongs to the compact class, has odd
\(m\), and satisfies
\[
 m|A_{ii}|^{m-1}\geq\kappa\quad(i\in V),
 \qquad
 |C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})|\geq\kappa\quad(j\to i\in E).
 \tag{1}
\]
The inclusions \(V_{uv}^{G}\subseteq V\) and
\(E_{uv}^{G}\subseteq E\), which follow directly from
\(\mathrm{def{:}target\mbox{-}corridor}\), show by restricting the two
minima in \((1)\) that
\[
 \mathfrak P_{\partial}\subseteq\mathfrak P_{uv,\partial}.
 \tag{2}
\]
Moreover, the hypotheses that the labels are topologically ordered, that
\(u\to v\in G\), and that
\(\kappa\leq m(1-\gamma)^{m-1}\), together with
\(\mathrm{lem{:}derivative\mbox{-}separated\mbox{-}class\mbox{-}nonempty}\),
give
\[
 \mathfrak P_{\partial}\neq\varnothing.
 \tag{3}
\]
Thus the class over which the asserted uniform limit is taken is
nonempty.

We next establish that the full and corridor estimators agree with
probability tending to one uniformly on \(\mathfrak P_{\partial}\).  The
needed neighborhood statement can be obtained directly from the compact
class conditions.  Indeed, a lower-triangular matrix in that class obeys,
for constants \(C_0<\infty\) and \(r_0\in(0,1)\) depending only on
\(d,\gamma,L\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}}\|A^r\|
 \leq C_0r_0^r,
 \qquad r\geq0.
 \tag{4}
\]
To verify \((4)\), expand an entry of \(A^r\) over nondecreasing index
walks.  Such a walk has at most \(d-1\) strict increases.  Its terms with
\(q\) strict increases are bounded by
\(L^q(1-\gamma)^{r-q}\), and their number is bounded by a constant times
\((r+1)^q\).  Summing over \(0\leq q\leq d-1\) and absorbing the resulting
fixed-degree polynomial into \(r_0^r/(1-\gamma)^r\), for any fixed
\(r_0\in(1-\gamma,1)\), proves \((4)\).

Stationarity and the innovation bounds in
\(\mathrm{def{:}compact\mbox{-}class}\) now give
\[
 M_0=\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}A^rD(A^r)^\top,
 \qquad
 d_{\min}I_d\preceq M_0\preceq C_1I_d,
 \tag{5}
\]
where \(C_1<\infty\) is uniform on \(\mathfrak P_{\partial}\).  Since
\(B=A^m\), the coarse autocovariances satisfy
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y_{s+k}Y_s^\top]=B^kM_0\quad(k\geq0),
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}}
 \|B^kM_0\|\leq C_2r_0^{mk}.
 \tag{6}
\]
For four coordinates of a centered jointly Gaussian vector,
differentiating its moment-generating function four times at zero gives
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(U_1U_2,U_3U_4)
 =\operatorname{Cov}(U_1,U_3)\operatorname{Cov}(U_2,U_4)
  +\operatorname{Cov}(U_1,U_4)\operatorname{Cov}(U_2,U_3).
 \tag{7}
\]
Applying \((7)\) to the entries of
\(Y_sY_s^\top\) and \(Y_sY_{s-1}^\top\), and then using \((6)\), yields
a constant \(C_3<\infty\) such that every scalar coordinate \(Z_s\) of
these two product arrays satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}}
 \sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}
 \bigl|\operatorname{Cov}_P(Z_0,Z_k)\bigr|\leq C_3.
 \tag{8}
\]
Consequently, by the definitions in
\(\mathrm{def{:}empirical\mbox{-}moments}\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
  \|\widehat M_0-M_0\|^2+\|\widehat M_1-M_1\|^2
 \right]
 \leq \frac{C_4}{n}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Here and below any fixed matrix norm may be used, since \(d\) is fixed.
The lower eigenvalue bound in \((5)\), the inverse identity
\(U^{-1}-V^{-1}=U^{-1}(V-U)V^{-1}\), and
\(B=M_1M_0^{-1}\) therefore imply
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}}P(\widehat M_0\not\succ0)
 \longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}}
 P\!\left(\|\widehat B-B\|>\delta\right)\longrightarrow0
 \quad\text{for every }\delta>0.
 \tag{10}
\]

At a population value from \(\mathfrak P_{\partial}\), the inverse
diagonal map \(b\mapsto b^{1/m}\) is differentiable at
\(b=A_{ii}^m\), with derivative
\[
 \frac{1}{mA_{ii}^{m-1}},
 \tag{11}
\]
whose absolute value is at most \(\kappa^{-1}\) by \((1)\).  Every
off-diagonal division in the full graph recursion has denominator of
absolute value at least \(\kappa\), again by \((1)\).  The parameter set
of matrices \(A\) described by the fixed entry, stability-margin, and
separation bounds is compact, and the recursion has finitely many steps.
Thus a finite induction over endpoint gap, using \((11)\) for diagonal
steps and ordinary continuity of addition, multiplication, and division
for edge steps, gives a single \(\delta_0>0\) such that whenever
\(\|\widetilde B-B\|<\delta_0\), both the full and corridor recursions are
defined in a common neighborhood of their population values and all
their displayed denominators have absolute value at least
\(\kappa/2\).  Let \(\mathcal E_n\) be this event with
\(\widetilde B=\widehat B\), together with
\(\widehat M_0\succ0\).  Equation \((10)\) gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}}P(\mathcal E_n^c)\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{12}
\]

On \(\mathcal E_n\), the full and corridor diagonal roots agree because
both are the unique real odd roots of the same entries \(\widehat B_{ii}\).
Now process an edge \(j\to i\in E_{uv}^{G}\) by increasing endpoint gap.
By
\(\mathrm{lem{:}target\mbox{-}corridor\mbox{-}recursion\mbox{-}closure}\),
every diagonal and strict-edge coordinate in its remainder lies in the
corridor, and every such strict edge has smaller endpoint gap.  Induction
therefore makes the numerator, denominator, and all previously recovered
inputs in the full and corridor updates identical.  Hence
\[
 \widehat A_{ij}^{\mathrm{full}}
 =\widehat A_{ij}^{\mathrm{cor}}
 \quad(j\to i\in E_{uv}^{G}),
 \qquad
 \widehat A_{vv}^{\mathrm{full}}=\widehat A_{vv}^{\mathrm{cor}}.
 \tag{13}
\]
Because \(u\to v\in E_{uv}^{G}\), \((13)\) and the two estimator
definitions imply, simultaneously for every \(z\in\mathcal Z\),
\[
 \widehat h_{uv}(z)
 =\widehat h_{uv}^{\mathrm{cor}}(z)
 =\frac{\widehat A_{vu}^{\mathrm{cor}}z}
 {1-\widehat A_{vv}^{\mathrm{cor}}z}.
 \tag{14}
\]
The computation of \(\widehat Q\) and the subsequent innovation-variance
recovery in the full procedure do not enter the last expression.

Equality \((14)\) holds as an identity of differentiable maps throughout
the common neighborhood defining \(\mathcal E_n\).  Therefore the target
rows of the full and corridor Jacobians are equal there, and those rows
have zero derivatives with respect to non-corridor recursion inputs.
Differentiating the final rational map gives, for either recursion,
\[
 \mathrm dh_{uv}(z)
 =\frac{z\,\mathrm dA_{vu}}{1-A_{vv}z}
  +\frac{A_{vu}z^2\,\mathrm dA_{vv}}{(1-A_{vv}z)^2}.
 \tag{15}
\]
The denominators in \((15)\) are nonzero because
\(|A_{vv}z|\leq1-\gamma<1\).  Since the two procedures use the same
estimated Gaussian lag-moment covariance, equality of their target
Jacobians implies on \(\mathcal E_n\) that
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_h=\widehat\Sigma_{h,\mathrm{cor}},
 \qquad
 \widehat c_{1-\alpha}
 =\widehat c_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{cor}}.
 \tag{16}
\]

By \((2)\),
\(\mathrm{thm{:}target\mbox{-}corridor\mbox{-}wald\mbox{-}band}\)
applies to every law in \(\mathfrak P_{\partial}\).  Equations
\((12)\), \((14)\), and \((16)\) show that the bounded-Lipschitz distance
between the laws of the full and corridor stacked, scaled transfer
vectors tends to zero uniformly on \(\mathfrak P_{\partial}\).  The same
theorem therefore gives the asserted centered Gaussian limit, with the
Jacobian in \((15)\).

Finally, let \(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{full}}\) and
\(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{cor}}\) be the simultaneous coverage events in the
present theorem and in the corridor theorem, respectively.  By
\((14)\) and \((16)\), they agree on \(\mathcal E_n\).  Hence
\[
\begin{split}
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}}
 \left|P(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{full}})-(1-\alpha)\right|
 &\leq
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}}
 \left|P(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{cor}})-(1-\alpha)\right|
 +\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}}P(\mathcal E_n^c)\\
 &\leq
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{uv,\partial}}
 \left|P(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{cor}})-(1-\alpha)\right|
 +\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_{\partial}}P(\mathcal E_n^c)
 \longrightarrow0,
\end{split}
 \tag{17}
\]
where the second inequality uses \((2)\), the first term tends to zero by
the target-corridor Wald theorem, and the second does so by \((12)\).
Together with \((3)\), this proves both the nonvacuity and every asserted
limit and coverage conclusion.
